note: Tracks refresh cadence and last-run timestamps per data type (not per ticker — per-ticker last_verified lives in targets.json). last_run is null until the corresponding fetch script has actually been run.

data_types.source: NOAA CPC ENSO Diagnostic Discussion; cross-check WMO/JMA/BOM/C3S
EU Commission (EUDR), NOAA/BOEM (deep-sea mining), state insurance regulators, USDA/India Ministry of Commerce

Aon '2026 Climate and Catastrophe Insight' report, Swiss Re sigma No. 1/2026, Gallagher Re Natural Catastrophe and Climate Report (full-year 2025, published Jan 21, 2026), and Munich Re's full-year 2025 nat-cat press release/factsheet (Jan 13, 2026) — all four flagged interested_party; not a live API, these are periodic published reports, manual research not a fetch script. All four now pulled from as of 2026-07-18. 3-of-4 corroborate on the 2025 global insured cat loss total (Aon $127B, Swiss Re ~$127B, Gallagher Re $129B); Munich Re diverges at $108B, a real ~16% methodological gap flagged rather than averaged away. The Jan 2025 Palisades/Eaton wildfire insured-loss figure has strong 4-way corroboration ($40-41B across all four sources).

data_types.cadence: quarterly (slow-moving multi-decadal trend, not a weekly mover)
data_types.source: NOAA CO-OPS tide gauge monthly means (local linear-regression trend)
NASA GISS Surface Temperature Analysis (GISTEMP v4)
NASA FIRMS (active-fire point detections, not perimeters — free MAP_KEY required)
